# ONE KITCHEN — source manuscript and stock

## Publication identity

- Title: ONE KITCHEN
- Subtitle: Four meals for one
- Author: Ellis Reed
- Publisher: Counterspace Press
- Copyright line: Copyright 2026 Counterspace Press
- Reader: one adult arranging four freshly prepared meals in a compact kitchen
- Publication: 20-page sample cookbook, including covers
- Trim: 170 × 240 mm
- Open-book footprint: 340 × 240 mm
- Clear worktop area: 420 × 320 mm
- Paper: 120 g/m² uncoated throughout
- Binding: saddle stitching
- Spine panel width: 0 mm
- Bleed: 3 mm
- Open spread including perimeter bleed: 346 × 246 mm
- Grid: two columns per page; 6 mm column gap
- Recipe identifier position: upper outer corner
- Recipe opening order: identifier and title; yield and tools; ingredients; numbered operations
- Front-cover emphasis: typography
- ISBN barcode area: blank 35 × 22 mm area at the lower right of page 20
- Chapter heading and graphic system: open design choices

## Editorial preparation record

| Item | Record |
|---|---|
| Completed manuscript work | Author arithmetic and ingredient-to-step checks |
| Physical cooking trials | Not undertaken |
| Chef approval | Not obtained |
| Nutritional review | Not undertaken |
| Recipe quantities | Original editorial amounts; individual intake requirements vary |
| Food information scope | Supplied ingredient records, operations, doneness cues, packet guidance and allergen wording |
| Cooking occasions | Determined by current package use-by and after-opening instructions |
| Meal identifiers | R1–R4; recipe identities rather than weekdays or a four-day storage schedule |
| Serving context | Each meal freshly prepared |
| Main stock calculation | R1–R4 once each at one portion |
| Two-portion comparison | Separate quantities for each doubled recipe |
| Diagram source | Recipe prose and the named ingredient-state changes |
| Illustration treatment | Original process diagrams and typographic explanations |

## Units and stock basis

- Inventory basis: one purchased pack or prepared portion per ingredient for the main four-meal plan; unbranded editorial quantities.
- Fresh vegetable basis: already washed, trimmed, edible weights; preparation loss already accounted for.
- Chickpea and lentil recipe basis: drained weights of already cooked canned pulses.
- Tomato basis: contents with juice, used without draining.
- Can records: total contents and usable drained weights recorded separately.
- Pita basis: pieces, each weighing 60 g; purchased pack of 2 pieces weighing 120 g total.
- Recipe food scope: the listed ingredients, garnishes and substitutions comprising the supplied manuscript; the listed recipes contain their complete food allocations.
- Tap water: separate cooking resource, outside purchased grocery stock.
- Seasoning inventory: olive oil, bottled lemon juice and ground cumin.
- Two-portion food arithmetic: each listed food amount × 2, retaining its unit and preparation basis; pita recorded by pieces and total mass.
- Two-portion stock basis: separate from the main one-pack inventory calculation.
- Cooking-water basis: the stated operation and relevant packet guidance.
- Pan capacity, doneness, heat and cooking time: operation-specific conditions, independent of the food-quantity multiplier.
- Reserved pasta water: a transfer from the original pasta cooking water, counted once.

## Available tools and illustration sources

| Tool | Fixed inventory |
|---|---|
| Hob | One active ring |
| Saucepan | One 2.5 L saucepan with lid |
| Frying pan | One 24 cm frying pan |
| Kettle | One electric kettle |
| Bowl | One 1 L heatproof bowl |
| Colander | One |
| Measuring jug | One 500 mL heatproof measuring jug, suitable for boiling water |
| Scale | Gram scale |
| Cutting board | One |
| Knife | One |
| Grater | One |
| Can opener | One |
| Fork | One |
| Spoon | One |
| Serving plate | One ordinary serving plate |
| Bowl cover | Serving plate or suitable lid |

- tool-reference.png: original schematic inventory illustration of the available equipment.
- Equipment capacities: publisher-supplied parameters; dimensional authority rests with these written records.
- R2 hob sequence: one saucepan used sequentially; one pan on the hob at a time.
- Appliance and utensil scope: the inventory above.
- Supplied illustration source material: tool-reference.png, recipe operations and named state changes.

## Food guidance and allergen copy

- Food Standards Agency cooking summary: relevant packet instructions, thorough cooking and sound preparation hygiene.
- Cooking completion basis: packet instructions and supplied doneness cues; completion time varies.
- GOV.UK storage summary: storage instructions remain relevant to a use-by date.
- Government allergen summary: wheat is among cereals containing gluten.
- Declared wheat products: couscous, pasta and pita.
- Product-label review scope: individual dietary requirements, possible additional ingredients and cross-contact information.
- Allergen statements: product-label prompts rather than exhaustive product allergen analyses.
- R3 product information: product labels remain the basis for identifying allergens in purchased ingredients.

| Recipe | Exact printed allergen statement |
|---|---|
| R1 | Contains wheat (gluten). Check every product label and your own dietary requirements. |
| R2 | Contains wheat (gluten). Check every product label and your own dietary requirements. |
| R3 | Check every product label and your own dietary requirements; this recipe is not an allergen-free guarantee. |
| R4 | Contains wheat (gluten). Check every product label and your own dietary requirements. |

## R1 — Chickpea and lemon couscous

- Yield: one portion.
- Pages: 6–7.
- Cooking water: starting amount 120 mL boiling water for hydration; quick-cooking couscous packet instructions take precedence for water amount and standing period.
- Water classification: process water, separate from purchased food allocation.
- Tools: kettle, heatproof bowl, fork, grater, knife and board, scale and heatproof measuring jug suitable for boiling water; serving plate or suitable lid as bowl cover.
- Hob occupancy: zero pans.

| Ingredient ID | Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| couscous | Plain quick-cooking wheat couscous | 75 g |
| chickpeas | Cooked plain canned chickpeas | 120 g |
| carrot | Washed and trimmed carrot | 80 g |
| pepper | Washed and trimmed sweet pepper | 75 g |
| oil | Olive oil | 10 mL |
| lemon | Bottled lemon juice | 15 mL |
| cumin | Ground cumin | 1 g |

| Step | Manuscript operation |
|---|---|
| R1.1 | Measure 75 g dry quick-cooking couscous into the heatproof bowl. Add 120 mL boiling water, cover with a suitable plate or lid and let hydrate according to its packet. Use a fork to check that the grains are tender; follow the packet if it requires a different water amount or standing period. |
| R1.2 | While the bowl stands, grate the 80 g prepared carrot and finely dice the 75 g prepared pepper. Drain the already cooked chickpeas and weigh 120 g drained beans. Check that the chosen canned product is suitable for eating without further cooking. |
| R1.3 | Fluff the tender couscous. Add the weighed chickpeas, carrot and pepper, then 10 mL olive oil, 15 mL lemon juice and 1 g cumin. Mix with the fork and serve freshly assembled. |

- Illustration state R1.1: dry quick-cooking couscous becoming hydrated, tender grain.
- Illustration state R1.2: already cooked canned chickpeas, drained and weighed to 120 g.

## R2 — Chickpea and tomato pasta

- Yield: one portion.
- Pages: 8–9.
- Cooking water: 1,000 mL for boiling pasta; 100 mL reserved from that same water before draining.
- Reserved-water classification: internal transfer, counted once within the original 1,000 mL.
- Tools: saucepan, colander, heatproof bowl, scale, heatproof measuring jug suitable for boiling water and spoon.
- Hob sequence: the same saucepan used sequentially on the single active ring.

| Ingredient ID | Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| pasta | Plain dried wheat pasta | 75 g |
| chickpeas | Cooked plain canned chickpeas | 120 g |
| tomatoes | Canned chopped tomatoes with juice | 200 g |
| onion | Peeled chopped onion | 80 g |
| oil | Olive oil | 10 mL |

| Step | Manuscript operation |
|---|---|
| R2.1 | Bring 1,000 mL water to the boil in the saucepan. Add 75 g dry pasta and cook according to its packet until cooked through. Before draining, measure 100 mL of this cooking water into the heatproof jug. Drain the pasta through the colander and transfer it to the heatproof bowl. |
| R2.2 | Return the empty saucepan to the hob. Heat 10 mL olive oil over medium heat; add 80 g prepared onion and stir until softened without burning. Lower the heat if necessary. |
| R2.3 | Add 200 g tomatoes including their juice, 120 g drained cooked chickpeas and the reserved 100 mL pasta water. Stir and simmer until the sauce and chickpeas are steaming hot throughout. |
| R2.4 | Return the pasta from the bowl to the saucepan. Toss until coated and thoroughly hot, then serve freshly cooked. Only one pan occupies the hob at any point. |

- Illustration state R2.1: 100 mL reserved-water branch before the colander; remaining draining liquid follows its separate disposal route.
- Illustration state R2.2: the same emptied saucepan returning to the hob.
- Water accounting: the reserve and the draining liquid are branches of the original cooking water.

## R3 — Lentil and carrot soup

- Yield: one portion.
- Pages: 10–11.
- Cooking water: 250 mL added to the soup.
- Tomato juice: already included in the 200 g tomato allocation.
- Tools: saucepan with lid, knife and board, scale, heatproof measuring jug suitable for boiling water and spoon; heatproof bowl for serving.
- Finished texture: chunky soup.
- Completion basis: fork-tender carrot and soup steaming hot throughout.

| Ingredient ID | Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| lentils | Cooked plain canned lentils | 120 g |
| carrot | Washed and trimmed carrot | 160 g |
| onion | Peeled chopped onion | 80 g |
| tomatoes | Canned chopped tomatoes with juice | 200 g |
| oil | Olive oil | 10 mL |
| cumin | Ground cumin | 1 g |

| Step | Manuscript operation |
|---|---|
| R3.1 | Cut 160 g prepared carrot into thin half-moons. Heat 10 mL olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the carrot and 80 g prepared onion; stir until the onion softens, lowering the heat if it catches. |
| R3.2 | Stir in 1 g cumin. Add 200 g tomatoes with their juice, 120 g drained cooked lentils and 250 mL water. Bring to a simmer and partly cover with the lid. |
| R3.3 | Simmer gently, stirring regularly, until the carrot is tender to a fork and the soup is steaming hot throughout. Serve the chunky soup freshly cooked in the heatproof bowl. |

- Illustration state R3.1: thin carrot half-moons.
- Illustration state R3.3: fork-tenderness check, with the soup retaining its chunky texture.

## R4 — Lentil and pepper pita

- Yield: one portion.
- Pages: 12–13.
- Cooking water: 40 mL for softening vegetables.
- Pita allocation: one ready-to-eat 60 g piece from the two-piece pack.
- Tools: frying pan, knife and board, grater, scale, heatproof measuring jug suitable for boiling water and spoon; ordinary serving plate.
- Pita preparation: ready-to-eat bread, split for filling.
- Serving allocation: all measured filling, divided between the pita and the same plate alongside it; one portion in total.

| Ingredient ID | Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| lentils | Cooked plain canned lentils | 120 g |
| pepper | Washed and trimmed sweet pepper | 75 g |
| carrot | Washed and trimmed carrot | 80 g |
| onion | Peeled chopped onion | 60 g |
| oil | Olive oil | 10 mL |
| lemon | Bottled lemon juice | 15 mL |
| cumin | Ground cumin | 1 g |
| pita | Plain ready-to-eat wheat pita | 1 piece (60 g) |

| Step | Manuscript operation |
|---|---|
| R4.1 | Grate 80 g prepared carrot and finely dice 75 g prepared pepper. Heat 10 mL olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat; add the carrot, pepper and 60 g prepared onion. Stir, add 40 mL water and cook until the vegetables soften, reducing the heat if necessary. |
| R4.2 | Stir in 1 g cumin and 120 g drained cooked lentils. Stir until the filling is steaming hot throughout. Remove the pan from the heat and stir in 15 mL lemon juice. |
| R4.3 | Split one ready-to-eat 60 g pita carefully. Spoon part of the hot filling into it without overfilling and serve the remaining filling alongside on the same plate. Serve freshly assembled; this is still one portion using all of the measured filling. |

- Illustration state R4.3: opening one pita piece and serving part of the filling alongside it; the entire measured filling remains visible in the serving allocation.

steps.userMessage:
ONE KITCHEN | A cookbook for four freshly prepared meals for one

We are publishing a 20-page sample cookbook for one adult cooking in a compact kitchen. Print the title "ONE KITCHEN" and subtitle "Four meals for one" on the front cover. The manuscript follows four freshly prepared meals: R1 Chickpea and lemon couscous, R2 Chickpea and tomato pasta, R3 Lentil and carrot soup, and R4 Lentil and pepper pita. R1–R4 identify meals; cooking occasions follow the purchased products' use-by and after-opening instructions. The shopping plan supplies each recipe once at one portion. A separate comparison gives two portions of each recipe. The available equipment includes one active hob ring, a 2.5 L saucepan, a 24 cm frying pan and a 1 L heatproof bowl; R2 uses the same saucepan sequentially.

Build the content outline and lookup rules first, then develop the publication around them. The format is 170 × 240 mm, with 20 pages including covers, 120 g/m² uncoated paper throughout, saddle stitching, a 0 mm spine panel and 3 mm bleed. The open book occupies 340 × 240 mm within a 420 × 320 mm clear worktop area. Use two columns per page, a 6 mm column gap, numbered recipe steps and original process diagrams. Recipe identifiers, yield and tools belong in consistent positions. The front cover should be led by typography. Credit author Ellis Reed and publisher Counterspace Press; the chapter spread carries the copyright line "Copyright 2026 Counterspace Press" and the supplied source credits.

Audience: adults living alone who need to move between shopping, ingredient allocation and cooking instructions, and the publishing team choosing the book's reading and lookup system.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the manuscript, stock, equipment, food guidance, fixed wording and page allocation. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables and their proportions, formats and stages. 03-quantity-records.en.md contains the one-portion allocation, remaining stock and separate two-portion quantities. kitchen-format.png is the constraint drawing for trim, bleed, binding and worktop footprint. tool-reference.png is the identity image of the existing equipment inventory. kitchen-counter.png is an atmosphere reference for reading an open book in a compact kitchen.

Deliverables:
1. One content outline and book standards document, with the complete 20-page allocation, lookup fields, step-number rules, two-column grid, type hierarchy, actual font names and production dimensions
2. One front cover, page 1, with title, subtitle, author and publisher
3. One contents and lookup introduction spread, pages 2–3, explaining the reading route and ingredient-to-recipe lookup
4. One chapter introduction spread, pages 4–5, with the equipment inventory, fresh-meal context, editorial preparation record, product-label guidance, copyright line and source credits
5. Four illustrated recipe spreads: R1 Chickpea and lemon couscous on pages 6–7; R2 Chickpea and tomato pasta on pages 8–9; R3 Lentil and carrot soup on pages 10–11; R4 Lentil and pepper pita on pages 12–13
6. One shopping index spread, pages 14–15, with all 12 purchased-stock records and distinct total and drained can weights
7. One allocation index spread, pages 16–17, with each ingredient's R1–R4 quantities, total use, remaining stock and recipe page references
8. One portion conversion spread, pages 18–19, comparing one and two portions for all four recipes, with food quantities and cooking-water notes
9. One back cover, page 20, with title, publisher, quick lookup for R1–R4 and a blank 35 × 22 mm ISBN barcode area at the lower right
10. One 12-second lookup video following chickpeas from the allocation index to R2 and its reserved-water operation
11. One presentation document of at least eight pages, reusing the outline, all eleven publication pieces and the video sequence, with the final book standards and actual font names

Acceptance:
- The outline and all publication pieces follow the 20-page allocation above. The contents, four recipe spreads and back-cover lookup repeat R1–R4 and their page pairs. Recipe spreads use two columns per page with a 6 mm gap, recipe identifiers at the upper outer corner, yield and tools before the ingredients, and step identifiers R1.1–R1.3, R2.1–R2.4, R3.1–R3.3 and R4.1–R4.3 beside the matching operations.
- The front cover prints ONE KITCHEN, Four meals for one, Ellis Reed and Counterspace Press. The back cover repeats ONE KITCHEN and Counterspace Press and places its 35 × 22 mm ISBN area at the lower right. The chapter spread prints Copyright 2026 Counterspace Press and the three supplied source credits with the access date 10 September 2026.
- The four recipe spreads carry every ingredient amount, operation and doneness cue in the manuscript. Their diagrams show R1's hydrated grain and 120 g drained chickpeas; R2's 100 mL reserve taken from its 1,000 mL cooking water before draining and the same saucepan returning to the hob; R3's thin carrot half-moons and fork-tenderness check; and R4's single 60 g pita with the remaining filling alongside.
- R1, R2 and R4 print "Contains wheat (gluten). Check every product label and your own dietary requirements." R3 prints "Check every product label and your own dietary requirements; this recipe is not an allergen-free guarantee." The chapter spread carries the manuscript's editorial preparation record and explains product-label checks, individual dietary requirements, additional ingredients and cross-contact information.
- The shopping and allocation spreads account for all 12 stock rows at one portion per recipe, including 240 g chickpeas used with 0 g remaining, 320 g carrot used with 80 g remaining, and one 60 g pita used with one 60 g pita remaining. The conversion spread doubles every food amount while retaining its unit and preparation basis, including R4's two pita pieces totaling 120 g; its cooking-water notes retain the manuscript's operation and packet guidance.
- The 12-second video visibly follows chickpeas on pages 16–17 to R2 on pages 8–9 and then to R2.1's 100 mL reserve. The presentation contains at least eight pages, reuses all eleven publication pieces, and repeats the outline's 170 × 240 mm trim, 20 pages, 0 mm spine panel, two columns per page, 6 mm gap, fixed cover wording and actual font names.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
